edges.reason: token() returns the state variable _token.
beneficiary() returns the state variable _beneficiary.
releaseTime() returns the state variable _releaseTime.
Constructor writes the token_ parameter into the _token immutable.
Constructor writes the beneficiary_ parameter into the _beneficiary immutable.
Constructor writes the releaseTime_ parameter into the _releaseTime immutable.
release() reads _token to query the contract balance and to build the outgoing transfer to an external contract.
release() sends the token balance to the _beneficiary address.
release() gates execution on block.timestamp >= releaseTime().
block.timestamp is compared against releaseTime() and therefore controls who may trigger the release.
Constructor requires releaseTime_ > block.timestamp, making deployment validity timestamp dependent.
getLockedAmount() queries the balanceOf of _token for this contract.
release() calls token().safeTransfer, which performs an external call to the token contract.
safeTransfer delegates the actual call to _callOptionalReturn, which performs a low-level external call.
_callOptionalReturn performs the call through the three-argument Address.functionCall.
_callOptionalReturn executes address(token).functionCall(data), handing control to the token contract.
A malicious token contract can call back into the SafeERC20 call path while returndata checking is pending.
The two-argument functionCall delegates to the three-argument overload.
functionCall(address,bytes,string) delegates to functionCallWithValue with value 0.
functionCallWithValue(address,bytes,uint256) delegates to the four-argument overload.
functionCallWithValue requires isContract(target) before performing the call.
functionCallWithValue performs target.call{value: value}(data), transferring all remaining gas and control.
The called contract can re-enter functionCallWithValue or its callers before the call returns.
functionCallWithValue passes the call outcome to verifyCallResult.
The two-argument functionStaticCall delegates to the three-argument overload.
functionStaticCall requires isContract(target) before performing the static call.
functionStaticCall performs target.staticcall(data) on an arbitrary contract.
The static-called contract executes its own logic and can interact with the caller's state reads.
The two-argument functionDelegateCall delegates to the three-argument overload.
functionDelegateCall requires isContract(target) before performing the delegate call.
functionDelegateCall performs target.delegatecall(data), executing external code in this contract context.
Delegatecalled code runs in this contract's storage context and can re-enter its entry points.
verifyCallResult reverts with raw returndata through inline assembly when the call failed.
sendValue performs recipient.call with value after only a balance check.
The recipient receives control with all gas and may re-enter sendValue or its callers.
release() triggers the external balanceOf and safeTransfer calls against the token contract.
A malicious token can re-enter release() during the transfer; the function has no reentrancy guard.
safeDecreaseAllowance computes oldAllowance - value inside an unchecked block.
safeApprove routes the encoded approve call through _callOptionalReturn.
safeTransferFrom routes the encoded transferFrom call through _callOptionalReturn.
safeIncreaseAllowance routes the encoded approve call through _callOptionalReturn.
